title: Apply for real estate tax relief for the elderly and disabled
question: I am 65 or older (or permanently disabled) and own my home. Can I get a break on my real estate tax?
office: Commissioner of the Revenue (City of Staunton)
summary: Staunton exempts some or all of the city real estate tax for homeowners who were 65 or older, or permanently and totally disabled, on December 31 of the prior year. You must hold title, alone or with others, on January 1 and live in the home as your only dwelling. Gross combined income of the owners and relatives living there must be $50,000 or less, and the owner's and spouse's net worth (not counting the home and up to one acre) $80,000 or less. The exemption is 100, 75, 50 or 25 percent, by income band. Apply to the Commissioner of the Revenue by May 1. No fee is stated. No source sets an appeal route; a denial can likely be contested with the Commissioner, then in circuit court.

legal_basis.quote: The governing body of any locality may, by ordinance, provide for the exemption from, deferral of, or a combination program of exemptions from and deferrals of taxation of real estate and manufactured homes

Such real estate shall be owned by, and be occupied as the sole dwelling of anyone at least 65 years of age or if provided in the ordinance, anyone found to be permanently and totally disabled as defined in § 58.1-3217
A dwelling jointly held by married individuals, with no other joint owners, may qualify if either spouse is 65 or over or is permanently and totally disabled
(ii) held in a revocable inter vivos trust over which the eligible person or the eligible person and his spouse hold the power of revocation

The governing body of the county, city, or town may, by ordinance, also provide for an exemption from or deferral of (or combination program thereof) real estate taxes for dwellings jointly held by two or more individuals not all of whom are at least age 65 or (if provided in the ordinance) permanently and totally disabled, provided that the dwelling is occupied as the sole dwelling by all such joint owners.

the General Assembly hereby authorizes the governing body of a county, city or town to establish by ordinance net financial worth or annual income limitations as a condition of eligibility for any exemption or deferral of tax allowed pursuant to this article.
except for those relatives living in the dwelling and providing bona fide caregiving services to the owner whether such relatives are compensated or not

net financial worth shall be based on adding together the net financial worth, including the present value of equitable interests, as of December 31 of the immediately preceding calendar year, of the owners, and of the spouse of any owner, of the dwelling.
may exempt or defer the real property taxes of the qualifying dwelling and the land, not exceeding ten acres, upon which it is situated.

No local ordinance shall require that a citizen reside in the jurisdiction for a designated period of time as a condition for qualifying for any real estate tax exemption or deferral program established pursuant to § 58.1-3210
a qualifying individual shall be required to either (i) pay all delinquent taxes, penalties, and interest assessed by the locality and incurred prior to becoming eligible for an exemption or deferral

The person claiming such exemption shall file annually with the commissioner of the revenue of the county, city or town assessing officer or such other officer as may be designated by the governing body in which such dwelling lies, on forms to be supplied by the county, city or town concerned
an affidavit or written statement setting forth (i) the names of the related persons occupying such real estate
a county, city or town may prescribe by ordinance for the filing of the affidavit or written statement on a three-year cycle with an annual certification by the taxpayer
the frequency with which an affidavit, written statement or certification as described in subsection B of this section must be filed
a certification by the Social Security Administration, the Department of Veterans Affairs or the Railroad Retirement Board

a sworn affidavit by two medical doctors who are either licensed to practice medicine in the Commonwealth or are military officers on active duty who practice medicine with the United States Armed Forces
The affidavit of at least one of the doctors shall be based upon a physical examination of the person by such doctor.
Such affidavit, written statement or certification shall be filed after January 1 of each year, but before April 1, or such later date as may be fixed by ordinance.
Such ordinance may include a procedure for late filing by first-time applicants or for hardship cases.
shall also make any other reasonably necessary inquiry of persons seeking such exemption, requiring answers under oath
The local governing body may, in addition, require the production of certified tax returns to establish the income or financial worth of any applicant for tax relief or deferral.

shall not be construed to mean that the real estate for which tax exemption or deferral is sought does not continue to be the sole dwelling of such persons during such extended periods of other residence so long as such real estate is not used by or leased to others for consideration.

may be granted for any year following the date that the qualifying individual occupying such dwelling and owning title or partial title thereto reaches the age of 65 years or for any year following the date the disability occurred.
shall nullify any exemption or deferral for the remainder of the current taxable year and the taxable year immediately following.
However, any locality may by ordinance provide (i) a prorated exemption or deferral for the portion of the taxable year during which the taxpayer qualified for such exemption or deferral
may nonetheless qualify for the current year by filing an affidavit that clearly shows a substantial change of circumstances

the term "permanently and totally disabled" shall mean unable to engage in any substantial gainful activity by reason of any medically determinable physical or mental impairment or deformity which can be expected to result in death or can be expected to last for the duration of such person's life.

steps.step: Check the age or disability test
steps.who: Homeowner (head of the household claiming the exemption)
steps.how: The head of the household must be 65 or older on December 31 of the year before the tax year. Someone under 65 qualifies only if permanently and totally disabled on that date. State law defines that as being unable to do any substantial gainful work because of a physical or mental impairment expected to last for life or to result in death. Under state law, a home owned jointly by a married couple with no other owners may qualify if either spouse meets the test (Va. Code § 58.1-3210(A)).
steps.deadline: 65 or older (or permanently and totally disabled) as of December 31 of the preceding year
steps.quote: The head of the household claiming the exemption is 65 or older as of December 31 of the preceding year, or, if under 65, is permanently and totally disabled as of that date.

steps.step: Check the ownership and home test
steps.how: You must hold title to the home, alone or with others, on January 1 of the tax year, and live there as your only dwelling. The home must be inside the City of Staunton. Under state law, a long stay in a hospital, nursing home or other care facility does not break the 'sole dwelling' rule, as long as the home is not used by or leased to others for consideration (Va. Code § 58.1-3214). A home in a revocable living trust that you (or you and your spouse) can revoke also counts. No minimum time living in the city may be required.
steps.deadline: Title held as of January 1 of the year for which the exemption is claimed
steps.quote: The title to the property is held or partially held by the person claiming the exemption as of January 1 of the year for which the exemption is claimed.

steps.how: Add up last calendar year's gross income from all sources of the owners who live in the home and of their relatives who live there. The total must be $50,000 or less. The first $2,500 of income from relatives other than the spouse is not counted. State law also leaves out relatives living in the home who provide bona fide caregiving to the owner, paid or not (Va. Code § 58.1-3212(A)); the city page does not mention this, so ask the office how it is applied.
steps.deadline: Income for the preceding calendar year
steps.quote: does not exceed $50,000 provided, however, that the first $2,500 of income from such relatives, other than the spouse, is not included.

steps.how: Add up the net worth of the owner and spouse on December 31, including equitable interests. Do not count the home itself or up to one acre of the land under it. The total must be $80,000 or less. Over $80,000, the table on the city page shows no exemption at any income.
steps.quote: The net combined financial worth of the owner and spouse, including equitable interests, but not including the value of the dwelling and up to one acre of land, as of December 31, does not exceed $80,000.

steps.step: Find the share of your real estate tax that would be exempt
steps.how: With net worth of $0 to $80,000, the city's table gives: gross combined income $0 to $27,500, 100 percent exempt; $27,501 to $35,000, 75 percent; $35,001 to $42,500, 50 percent; $42,501 to $50,000, 25 percent. The Taxes page lists the real estate tax rate as $0.91 per $100 of assessed value.
steps.quote: Using the table below, you can determine the amount of exemption for which you would be eligible.

steps.step: If you are under 65, get proof of permanent and total disability
steps.who: Homeowner (applicant); Social Security Administration, Department of Veterans Affairs or Railroad Retirement Board, or two medical doctors
steps.how: State law requires a certification from the Social Security Administration, the Department of Veterans Affairs or the Railroad Retirement Board, attached to the form. Only if you are not eligible for certification by any of those agencies may you attach instead a sworn affidavit from two medical doctors licensed in Virginia (or active-duty military doctors) that you are permanently and totally disabled, at least one of them based on a physical examination. A Social Security disability certification counts as long as you stay eligible for those benefits. The city page does not list the documents, so ask the office what to attach.
steps.quote: a certification by the Social Security Administration, the Department of Veterans Affairs or the Railroad Retirement Board

steps.how: Download the Tax Relief application from the city's Tax Relief FAQs page, or go to the Commissioner of Revenue's office on the first floor of City Hall, 116 W. Beverley Street, and apply in person. State law says the filing is an affidavit or written statement on the city's own form. It names the related people living in the home and states that combined income and net worth are within the limits.
steps.quote: You can download the application or visit the Commissioner of Revenue’s office on the first floor of City Hall, 116 W. Beverley Street to apply in person.

steps.step: File the application with the Commissioner of the Revenue by May 1
steps.who: Homeowner (applicant), to the Commissioner of the Revenue
steps.how: Turn in the completed application, with any disability proof, at the Commissioner of Revenue's office in City Hall (hours 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.). The office's mailing address is P.O. Box 4, Staunton, VA 24402, but the page does not say whether a mailed application is accepted, so call 540.332.3829 to check. State law sets a January 1 to April 1 window unless the ordinance sets a later date; Staunton's date is May 1. State law requires a yearly filing unless the ordinance sets a three-year cycle with yearly certification or otherwise sets how often to file (Va. Code § 58.1-3213(A) to (C)); the city page does not say which applies.
steps.quote: The deadline to apply is May 1.

steps.step: If you missed May 1, ask about late filing
steps.how: State law lets a city ordinance set a late-filing procedure for first-time applicants or hardship cases. Staunton's code has a section titled 'Provision for late filing' (City Code § 3.15.100), but its text was not read and the city page does not describe it. Call the Commissioner's office at 540.332.3829 and ask.
steps.quote: Such ordinance may include a procedure for late filing by first-time applicants or for hardship cases.

steps.step: The Commissioner reviews the claim and makes any further inquiry needed
steps.how: State law directs the Commissioner to make any other reasonably necessary inquiry of the applicant, requiring answers under oath, to decide whether you qualify, including whether you are permanently and totally disabled. The city may also require certified tax returns to prove income or net worth. Staunton's code has a section titled 'Inquiries by commissioner' (City Code § 3.15.040; text not read). The city page warns that other provisions of the program can affect eligibility and asks applicants to call the office for details.
steps.quote: shall also make any other reasonably necessary inquiry of persons seeking such exemption, requiring answers under oath

steps.step: The exemption reduces your real estate tax; pay any remaining tax to the Treasurer
steps.who: Commissioner of the Revenue; City Treasurer
steps.how: The approved percentage comes off the year's city real estate tax. The city's pages do not describe how the exemption shows on the bill. Any tax still owed is paid to the City Treasurer: three quarters by June 20 and one quarter by December 5. If a due date falls on a day the office is closed, payment the next business day carries no penalty. For help paying, call the Treasurer's office at 540.332.3833. Staunton's code has a section titled 'Forfeiture of exemption for failure to pay taxes' (City Code § 3.15.080; text not read), so ask the office how unpaid tax affects the exemption.
steps.quote: June 20, ¾ due; Dec. 5, ¼ due

steps.step: Report changes during the year, and apply again for later years
steps.how: Under state law, a change during the year in income, net worth, ownership or other factors that breaks the limits ends the exemption for the rest of that year and the next, unless the ordinance prorates it. Staunton's code has a section titled 'Changes affecting exemption' (City Code § 3.15.070; text not read), so tell the office about any change. Apply again by May 1 each year unless the office tells you otherwise. Staunton's code also has a 'False claims' section (§ 3.15.090; text not read).
steps.quote: shall nullify any exemption or deferral for the remainder of the current taxable year and the taxable year immediately following.

escalation.trigger: Relief denied, or the exemption percentage seems wrong, so too much real estate tax is charged
escalation.next: Commissioner of the Revenue: apply for correction of the erroneous assessment
escalation.deadline: Within three years from the last day of the tax year, or within one year from the date of the assessment, whichever is later (Va. Code § 58.1-3980(A))
escalation.quote: Sections 58.1-3980 through 58.1-3983 shall also apply to erroneous assessments of real estate if the error sought to be corrected in any case was made by the commissioner of the revenue or such other official to whom the application is made

escalation.trigger: The Commissioner acts on your correction request and you want the reasons in writing
escalation.next: Commissioner of the Revenue: written statement of the facts and law, on request
escalation.quote: if so requested by the applicant, the commissioner or other such official shall state in writing the facts and law supporting the action on such application and mail a copy of such writing to the applicant at his last known address.

escalation.trigger: The Commissioner agrees the charge is improper or an obvious error but cannot correct it under § 58.1-3981
escalation.next: The Commissioner applies to the circuit court for the taxpayer's relief
escalation.quote: the commissioner of the revenue or other assessing official shall apply to the appropriate court, in the manner herein provided for relief of the taxpayer.

escalation.trigger: Correction refused or no decision from the Commissioner; § 58.1-3984(A) does not require a prior application to the Commissioner, so the owner may also apply to the court directly
escalation.next: Circuit Court of the City of Staunton: application to correct an erroneous assessment
escalation.deadline: Within three years from the last day of the tax year, one year from the assessment, or one year from the Commissioner's final determination under § 58.1-3981, whichever is later (Va. Code § 58.1-3984(A))
escalation.quote: apply for relief to the circuit court of the county or city wherein such assessment was made

escalation.trigger: The homeowner is a veteran rated 100 percent service-connected, permanently and totally disabled (or a qualifying surviving spouse)
escalation.next: Disabled veterans real estate tax exemption (state-mandated; Staunton City Code ch. 3.17), a separate exemption with its own application
escalation.quote: the General Assembly hereby exempts from taxation the real property, including the joint real property of married individuals, of any veteran who has been rated by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs or its successor agency pursuant to federal law to have a 100 percent service-connected, permanent, and total disability

caveats: The City of Staunton's website (www.ci.staunton.va.us) refuses automated readers, so the city pages and PDFs cited here are Internet Archive copies: they show the pages as they were when copied. The Tax Relief FAQs text is the same in the copies of 2025-04-17, 2025-08-15, 2026-01-23, 2026-02-09, 2026-06-15 and 2026-07-17 (the latest the Internet Archive holds), but the live page as of October 2026 is not confirmed. The live pages may have changed since; confirm on them or by phone before you act.

The application (form f1) is not confirmed: the city site refuses automated readers and the Internet Archive holds no copy. Its questions, required attachments, signature or notary requirement, and any mailing instructions are not verified. The version number in the URL suggests the file was posted on 2026-01-05 (an inference from the URL; an earlier version, document 12861, was posted on 2025-01-27). Expect a new URL for the 2027 filing season. A copy of a 2023 Staunton application on a private website is not official and is not used.

Local ordinance not quoted. Staunton's City Code is published on General Code's eCode360, whose Terms and Conditions of Use limit its content to personal use and forbid reproducing it for public purposes, so no City Code text is quoted here. Its Title 3 table of contents records Chapter 3.15 (Real Estate Tax Exemption for Elderly and Disabled Persons): § 3.15.010 Definitions; § 3.15.020 Authorized; § 3.15.030 General eligibility requirements; § 3.15.040 Inquiries by commissioner; § 3.15.050 Claimant's affidavit and certificate of disability, Commissioner's certification; § 3.15.060 Amount of exemption; § 3.15.070 Changes affecting exemption; § 3.15.080 Forfeiture of exemption for failure to pay taxes; § 3.15.090 False claims; § 3.15.100 Provision for late filing (https://ecode360.com/49100171, with sections at https://ecode360.com/49100172 through https://ecode360.com/49100193). The older Code Publishing Company copy (codepublishing.com/VA/Staunton/) refuses automated readers. Local rules here come from the city's own Tax Relief FAQs page, not from the code text.

Limits changed. The April 2023 capture of the city page gave a $35,000 income limit, a $70,000 net worth limit and a different percentage table. The April 2025 and later captures give $50,000 and $80,000. The amending ordinance was not found, and the city's agendas and minutes could not be read (same 403).

Filing frequency. The city page says only 'The deadline to apply is May 1.' It does not say whether a full application is needed every year or whether a three-year cycle with yearly recertification applies (Va. Code § 58.1-3213(A), (B)). The state default is a yearly filing.

How to submit. The page names two ways to apply: download the application, or apply in person at the office. It does not say whether a downloaded application may be mailed, faxed or dropped off. The office's mailing address and fax are recorded from the Commissioner of Revenue page; confirm with the office before relying on mail or fax.

Late filing, changes, unpaid taxes and false claims. City Code §§ 3.15.100, 3.15.070, 3.15.080 and 3.15.090 cover these, but their text was not read. Va. Code § 58.1-3212(B) lets a locality require, as a condition of relief, that delinquent taxes, penalties and interest be paid, put on an installment agreement of up to 72 months, or settled by an offer in compromise accepted by the Treasurer. Whether and how Staunton does this (the heading of § 3.15.080 refers to forfeiture for failure to pay taxes) is not confirmed. The penalty for a false claim is not stated here.

Income counting. The city page counts the income of owners living in the home and of their relatives living there, excluding 'the first $2,500 of income from such relatives, other than the spouse'. It does not say whether that $2,500 applies per relative or in total. Va. Code § 58.1-3212(A) leaves out relatives living in the home who provide bona fide caregiving to the owner, paid or not. The city page does not mention that exclusion, and the state rule likely controls; ask the office. (When the state exclusion was enacted was not established: the index text lists 2025 amendments, cc. 522 and 536, but does not show what they changed.)
Land. The page leaves the dwelling and up to one acre out of net worth. It does not say how much land the exemption itself covers. State law allows up to ten acres (Va. Code § 58.1-3212(A)).

Co-owners. The page accepts title 'held or partially held' by the claimant. Whether Staunton prorates the exemption when a co-owner other than a spouse is under 65 and not disabled (a local option under Va. Code § 58.1-3211.1) is not stated.

Disability proof. The city page does not list what to attach for an applicant under 65. The documents in step s6 come from Va. Code § 58.1-3213(D); City Code § 3.15.050's heading refers to a certificate of disability.

The table on the city page has a typo ('$27.501') for the start of the 75 percent band; it is read as $27,501. Its '$80,000 +' net worth column shows 0 percent at every income. The page describes an exemption only; no deferral program was found.
Tax rate. The Taxes page gives $0.91 per $100 in both the 2026-02-16 and 2026-08-22 captures, with the same June 20 and December 5 due dates. The adopted 2026 rate ordinance was not read.

Change of circumstances. Va. Code § 58.1-3215(C) lets an ordinance allow someone who was over last year's income or net worth limits to qualify for the current year by an affidavit clearly showing a substantial change of circumstances that was not volitional. Whether Staunton allows this is not stated on the city page; ask the office.

Escalation is inferred. Neither Article 2 of Chapter 32 of Title 58.1 nor the city page sets an appeal route for a refused exemption, and Chapter 3.15 was not read. The route shown is the general correction process for erroneous local assessments made by the Commissioner (Va. Code §§ 58.1-3980, 58.1-3981, 58.1-3984). Disputes about the assessed value of the property go to the City Assessor and the Board of Equalization instead, a separate process. The administrative appeal in Va. Code § 58.1-3983.1 covers local business and mobile property taxes, not this exemption. No deadline for the Commissioner to decide an application was found in Article 2 or in §§ 58.1-3980 to 58.1-3984.

Va. Code § 58.1-3211 (restrictions and conditions) is missing from Open US Law's copy of the Code of Virginia, so it is not quoted. Read https://law.lis.virginia.gov/vacode/58.1-3211/ before relying on it.
No fee for applying is stated on the city page, and state law sets none. The fees list is left empty.

Entry point. The city's 'I Want To > Apply For > Tax Relief' menu link (https://www.ci.staunton.va.us/i-want-to-/apply-for/tax-relief) answered with a redirect in the Internet Archive captures from 2018 to 2026-07-17 (two November 2021 captures excepted); the July 2026 redirect goes to a navigation id whose target was not resolved. The Local Tax Forms page (capture of 2026-02-15) does not list the tax relief application.

Privacy. The Commissioner of Revenue page names the elected Commissioner and links a personal staff mailbox. Those are omitted. No general office mailbox for the Commissioner was found, so only the office phone, fax, addresses and page are recorded.

Staunton is an independent city surrounded by Augusta County. Some homes with a Staunton mailing address are in Augusta County and are taxed by the county, so the city's program does not cover them. Check that the home is inside city limits.

corrections: Quotes: all 37 state-law quotes (28 in legal_basis, including the one added for § 58.1-3213(C); 4 in steps; 5 in escalation) are whitespace-normalised substrings of I.text_of for the cited section, and each falls in the cited subsection. All 16 city quotes match the Internet Archive captures of the cited pages word for word (Tax Relief FAQs 2025-04-17, 2026-02-09, 2026-06-15 and 2026-07-17, identical text; Taxes page 2026-02-16 and 2026-08-22). None removed.

Summary: 'exempts part of' changed to 'exempts some or all of' (the table goes up to 100 percent). The escalation sentence now says no source sets an appeal route and that a denial can likely be contested with the Commissioner, then in circuit court; the draft stated it as fact.

s1: the married-couple rule said couples 'qualify'. Va. Code § 58.1-3210(A) says a dwelling jointly held by married individuals with no other joint owners 'may qualify' if either spouse meets the test.

s2: the care-facility exception now uses the statute's condition, that the home is 'not used by or leased to others for consideration' (§ 58.1-3214); the draft said 'not rented or used by others for pay'.

s3: added the state-law exclusion of relatives living in the home who provide bona fide caregiving to the owner (§ 58.1-3212(A), which says the income computation 'shall be based' on that rule); the city page does not mention it.

s6: the two-doctor affidavit is allowed only if the person 'is not eligible for certification' by SSA, VA or the Railroad Retirement Board (§ 58.1-3213(D)); the draft said 'If you cannot get one of those'. Added that the affidavit must state the person is permanently and totally disabled.
s8: filing frequency now also cites § 58.1-3213(C), which lets the ordinance set how often to file; legal_basis entry added for that clause.

s10: the draft said the Commissioner 'may ask' further questions. § 58.1-3213(F) says the Commissioner 'shall also make any other reasonably necessary inquiry', requiring answers under oath. Step title and text changed.

s11: source moved to the 2026-08-22 Taxes capture (same due dates and $0.91 rate). The Treasurer's office phone 540.332.3833 is confirmed by the City Treasurer page (capture 2026-07-17); the contact now cites that page. Added a pointer to the City Code § 3.15.080 heading on forfeiture for unpaid taxes.
Escalation rung 4: § 58.1-3984(A) does not require a prior application to the Commissioner, so the trigger now says the owner may also go to court directly.

Caveat on caregiving relatives: removed the claim that the exclusion dates from 2025 (cc. 522, 536). The index text lists those acts in the section history but does not show what they changed, and the verified Albemarle file reports that the county's 2019 ordinance text already mirrors the exclusion.
Caveat on § 58.1-3212(B): added the offer-in-compromise option and the 72-month cap on installment agreements, which the statute lists.

Caveats updated: access (2026-06-15 capture added; verifier re-check of the 403 on 2026-10-11), tax rate (still $0.91 in the 2026-08-22 capture), the menu entry point (it redirects in captures through 2026-07-17), and escalation scope (§ 58.1-3983.1 covers business and mobile property taxes; the 'no deadline' statement narrowed to the sections searched). Added a caveat on the § 58.1-3215(C) change-of-circumstances option.
